title: As a power-user, I can write and format notes with headings, callouts, tables, code blocks, and embedded media in a fast keyboard-driven editor
As a power-user, I can define reusable templates (with variables like date and title) and apply them when creating recurring kinds of notes
As a power-user, I get an automatic daily note for each day, pre-filled from a template, as the default landing place for journaling and capture
As a researcher, I can clip web pages, articles, and highlights from my browser straight into my notes with an official clipper or capture flow
As a researcher, I can link notes with [[wiki-style]] links and see every backlink and unlinked mention of a note in context
As a power-user, I can reference or transclude an individual block or section of one note inside another and have it stay in sync
As a researcher, I can explore my knowledge base as an interactive graph of notes and connections, filtered to what I care about
As a researcher, I can instantly search all my notes with full-text search plus filters on tags, properties, and paths — including offline
As a power-user, I can query my notes by their structured properties and render live database-style views (tables, boards, lists) from those queries
As a power-user, I can attach typed properties and tags to notes and use them consistently for organization and retrieval
As a power-user, my notes live in local files or a local-first store that I own and can read without the app, and everything keeps working fully offline
As a researcher, my notes are stored or exportable in open, documented formats (Markdown, JSON) so my archive outlives the vendor
As a developer, I can run the whole system without the vendor's cloud — local-only mode or a self-hosted sync backend I operate myself
As a power-user, I can browse and install from a large catalog of community plugins/extensions to add features the core app doesn't ship
As a developer, I can build my own plugins against a documented extension API/SDK with samples and developer docs
As a developer, I can drive the app from outside — create or open notes via a URI scheme, deep links, or a local endpoint — to wire it into my scripts and workflows
As a power-user, an official sync service keeps my notes updated across all my devices with end-to-end encryption the vendor can't read
As a researcher, I can share a vault or space with collaborators and edit notes together without stepping on each other's changes
As a power-user, I can view a note's version history and restore earlier versions or recover deleted notes
As a researcher, I can publish selected notes as a browsable website — a digital garden with working links — without leaving the app
As a switcher, I can import my existing notes from Notion, Evernote, Roam, or plain Markdown with structure, links, and attachments preserved
As a switcher, I can export my entire knowledge base at any time in open formats, so leaving is as easy as arriving
As a power-user, full-featured iOS and Android apps give me my whole knowledge base — capture, search, and linking — not a stripped-down companion
As an AI-native user, a built-in AI assistant can answer questions, summarize, and draft grounded in my own notes — with clear controls over what data it sees
As an AI-native user, I can connect external LLMs and AI tools to my notes through first-party connectors or an ecosystem of AI plugins
As an AI-native user, my coding agent or assistant can read AND write my notes headlessly — through a documented local API, vendor API, or MCP server — without me touching the GUI
